findings.topic: case deadlines are specified but not enforceable from the contract
findings.evidence: The contract assigns the integration case a 240-second timeout and ordinary cases 30 seconds, and the gate requires those limits. It only defines a 300-second pytest-phase timeout as an execution watchdog. It does not specify a per-case watchdog or propagated monotonic deadline that bounds the full integration test, nor how test timeout expiry interrupts a blocking worker/client subprocess and proceeds to owned-process cleanup. Individual readiness, probe, and shutdown limits can accumulate beyond 240 seconds, so those component bounds do not establish the integration-case bound.
findings.required_resolution: Amend the contract to state how each test's full elapsed time is enforced before execution (including the integration's 240-second deadline), how remaining budget is passed to blocking subprocess/RPC operations, and how expiry triggers exact-handle termination/reaping while preserving failure evidence. The subsequent source pre-gate review must verify the implementation follows that pinned mechanism.
